clue.text: Saying gold is snatched in unfortunate mishap

indicators.note: something snatched in is held inside another piece, so the gold sits within the jumbled word
an unfortunate mishap is one that goes wrong, so its letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A proverb about a jeweller whose gold is stolen in some unlucky accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' tells you to jumble the mishap; the gold goes in midway. OR, heraldic gold, is a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorism is a pithy maxim, the kind of short wise remark people call a saying.

clue.text: Appearance of warped space-time

indicators.note: something warped is bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time in physics

explanation.surface: How warped space-time looks to an astronomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warped' rearranges SPACE plus T, the symbol for time.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the way something looks, its outward look or facet.

clue.text: German poet, one grasping most of poem's feature

parts.note: a holder is one who grasps or holds something

indicators.note: most of means the word drops its final letter

parts.note: a line is a basic feature of any poem

explanation.surface: A German poet clutching most of a verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims LINE to LIN. Friedrich Hölderlin was a German Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Hölderlin wrote lyric verse around 1800, a major Romantic writer of Germany.

clue.text: Disruption's disturbing in court

indicators.note: disturbing the letters throws them out of order

explanation.surface: A disruption is upsetting proceedings in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' rearranges INCOURT; the 's after 'Disruption' stands for 'is' and links.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy row or commotion, a disturbance of the peace.

clue.text: Scorch-mark's a source of information, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a singer is underworld slang for an informer who sings to the police

explanation.surface: A burn mark proves to be mostly a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: An informer 'sings' to the police, so a SINGER is a source of information; 'mostly' drops its R. The 's after 'Scorch-mark' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A singe is a slight surface burn, the light mark left by scorching.

clue.text: Yesterday's meat seen in northern town

parts.note: yesterday's things are old, past their best
ham is a cured pork meat

explanation.surface: Stale leftover meat on offer in a town in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: OLDHAM is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham is a Lancashire mill town near Manchester, so it is a town of the English north.

clue.text: Drunk trapped in awkward hole in African country

indicators.note: trapped in says these letters are held inside another piece
awkward means clumsy and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A drunk stuck down a nasty pit somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an adjective for someone in the hole, but it is the noun, a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a mountain kingdom ringed by South Africa, a nation in southern Africa.

clue.text: Chap embraces a German poet

indicators.note: embraces says the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a chap
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A man hugging a German poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a German' is not a German person but the German word for 'a'. Heinrich Heine was a nineteenth-century German poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Heine was a nineteenth-century German writer of lyric verse.

clue.text: Big name gossip seized on by me and sailor

indicators.note: seized on by means held inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: taken as written
tar is an old word for a sailor
gas is idle chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: Celebrity gossip gets snapped up by me and a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gossip' here is idle talk, which the slangy 'gas' also means.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is a hugely famous performer, a celebrity of the top rank.

clue.text: Resort — British? Absolutely!

parts.note: right on is an exclamation of hearty agreement

explanation.surface: Is this seaside resort British? Absolutely it is!
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside resort on the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a seaside town in Sussex, a holiday destination by the sea.

clue.text: Pedestrian aid eclipsing no cars, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A road crossing so quiet that it seems to blot out the traffic entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the fifteen letters of ECLIPSING NO CARS. A PELICAN CROSSING is a British pedestrian crossing with lights the walker controls by a button.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelican crossing is a signal-controlled place to cross the road, a help to people on foot.

clue.text: Undergarment's cambric hem is easily trimmed on both sides

indicators.note: trimming the words at each end leaves a run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: A seamstress notes that the hem of a cambric slip is easy to cut back at each edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut the phrase 'cambric hem is easily' at both ends and CHEMISE is left inside it; the 's after 'Undergarment' stands for 'is' and links.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemise is a loose shift worn next to the skin, a piece of lingerie.

clue.text: Timid attempt to clip wings of teal

indicators.note: to clip here is to grip, as a clip holds, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a guess is an attempt at an answer

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A nervous bid to clip the wings of a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings of teal' gives T and L, its first and last letters, and 'to clip' sets them inside GUESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gutless lacks courage, which is to say they are fearful and spineless.

clue.text: Frame for drugs offence using feature of garden?

definitions.meaning: to plant cannabis on someone frames them for a drugs crime
a container for growing flowers, found in many gardens

explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase, planting pot means framing someone with cannabis; as one item, it is a flower container in a garden.

clue.text: Think about mother's source of scent

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to ponder is to think over
ma is a word for mother

explanation.surface: Considering a mother's perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of scent' is a fair definition: a pomander is carried to give off fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomander is a ball of spices or perfume carried or hung to give off fragrance.

clue.text: Love for each one in dramatic presentation

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
per means for each, as in per person
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Romantic love for every single person in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music, a theatrical performance.

clue.text: Supplier of line bound to provide enhancement for viewers?

definitions.text: Supplier of line bound to provide enhancement for viewers?

parts.words: Supplier of line bound to provide enhancement for viewers?
parts.note: viewers are eyes, and the make-up that colours the lids above them enhances them, drawing a shaded line along their border

explanation.surface: A company providing a cable link to improve the picture for television audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' suggests a TV audience, but it means eyes; the make-up shades a line along the lid that borders them.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is cosmetic colour brushed on the eyelids to make the eyes look more striking.

clue.text: Sign of success — hitches finished with?

definitions.meaning: a raised-thumb gesture means all is well
a hitch-hiker's thumbs go away once the hitches are over, read as thumbs being up, finished

explanation.definitionFit: The raised-thumb gesture signals approval, and up can mean over, so a hitch-hiker's thumbs are done with.

clue.text: Workers exhibiting extremes of hopelessness

parts.note: the extreme letters of the word for despair are its first and last, an H and an S

explanation.surface: Labourers who show the depths of despair.
explanation.walkthrough: The extremes, first and last letters, of 'hopelessness' are H and S; said as 'H and S' they run together into the answer. 'exhibiting' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands is an old term for manual labourers, as in farm hands or deck hands.

clue.text: Astronomy, say, since rubbished by church

indicators.note: something rubbished is wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Astronomy, for example, has been dismissed by the church ever since.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbished' rearranges SINCE to SCIEN, followed by CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy is one of the natural sciences, an example of systematic study of the world.

clue.text: Reverend gentleman seen around Northern Ireland

indicators.note: around signals that one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: Mister is the title of a gentleman

explanation.surface: A clergyman spotted touring Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is a link word; 'Reverend' alone is the definition, used as a noun for a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, often addressed as the Reverend.

clue.text: Betray a successful performance

definitions.meaning: to betray one's side or principles
a show for which every ticket goes

explanation.definitionFit: Selling out means betraying a cause, and a show is a sell-out when every seat is booked.

clue.text: Sailors tucking into meat, such as lamb, traditionally?

indicators.note: tucking into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: veal is meat from calves
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors eating meat, lamb for instance, as tradition demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' tempts as more meat, but it belongs to the definition: lambs are born in spring, the vernal season.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal means of the spring, the season traditionally linked with newborn lambs.

clue.text: Skill I observed in a male extraterrestrial

indicators.note: observed in says these letters are seen inside the next piece

parts.note: a man is a male person
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A clever being spotted in a man turns out to be an alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a male' gives the whole word for a man, and the skill and the I go inside it together.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martian is a being from Mars, an alien from beyond Earth.

clue.text: Car turns

explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls is a Rolls-Royce automobile, and rolling is turning over and over.

clue.text: Disruptive and disgusting person back? Flee

indicators.note: back says the word for the disgusting person is read the other way

parts.note: a slob is a lazy and slovenly person
hie is an old word for hurry or go quickly

explanation.surface: A troublemaker and an unpleasant type is coming back, so run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SLOB into BOLS; HIE, an archaic verb for hasten, is stretched to mean flee. BOLSHIE is British slang for stroppy and uncooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie means rebellious and awkward, someone who causes trouble for authority.

clue.text: Cane a bottom around start of term

indicators.note: around says one piece goes round the other

parts.note: the base is the bottom of something

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Beating a backside at the start of the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of term' gives T, which BASE goes 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste someone is to beat or thrash them, as a cane would.

clue.text: Describing mum's Olympic success?

parts.note: mum here means keeping quiet, and an Olympic success is a gold medal, so the proverb is read as a quiet person winning gold

explanation.surface: A proud account of a mother's medal at the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother, but in 'keep mum' it means silent; the proverb is read as if silence had won a gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb praises keeping quiet, and the clue reads it as quietness winning first place at the Games.

clue.text: Chap trapping second badger

indicators.note: trapping says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Peter is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A man catches a badger in the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapping' puts S inside PETER; 'badger' is the verb, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to nag them persistently, harassing them with demands.

clue.text: Kitchen item, tall object, mostly, in shade of greenish-blue

indicators.note: in says the trimmed word goes inside the colour

parts.note: teal is a blue-green colour

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tower is a tall building

explanation.surface: A tall object in the kitchen, painted a blue-green shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tall object' is a tower, cut short by 'mostly'; 'in' then sets it within the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea towel is a cloth for drying dishes, found by every kitchen sink.
